title: Work plan and resources
content:
# B.3.1 Work plan and resources

## Overall structure

The action is a Research and Innovation Action with a single EU contribution of EUR 5,000,000 per project. It runs over an assumed 48-month duration and is organised into seven work packages, 35 tasks and 24 deliverables. WP1 (Coordination, governance and the interoperability interface, lead P01) holds governance and the external coordination duties. WP2 (Knowledge gaps, data needs and the integration architecture, lead P02) prioritises the gaps and specifies the architecture. WP3 (Joint protocols, metadata and interoperability crosswalks, lead P10) turns the architecture into agreed protocols and crosswalks. WP4 (Demonstration and verification cases along the pressure gradient, lead P03) runs the three realm cases. WP5 (The omics and molecular observation layer, lead P09) joins the molecular record to the in-situ and remote-sensing record. WP6 (Training resources, habitat mapping and trend prediction, lead P12) builds the training resource, the classifiers and the European-scale maps. WP7 (Policy uptake, sectoral mainstreaming and exploitation, lead P05) carries the indicators to competent authorities and to agricultural holdings.

The design is sequential where the science requires it. The gap analysis precedes the architecture. The protocols precede the campaigns, so a case run under a protocol that changes later does not produce data the other cases cannot join. The three realm campaigns run in sequence, so each one tests whether an upstream harmonisation decision survives transfer. Model training, European scaling and exploitation follow the case datasets.

Every partner participation is unconfirmed and carried as an operator assumption. Six partners (P07 to P12) are declared gap partners whose participation no confirmed source evidences. The freshwater case rests on P07 alone and the marine case on P08 alone, so losing either removes a realm rather than delaying it (risks R01 and R02).

## Timing (Gantt at deliverable granularity)

The canonical reference pack fixes deliverable due months but not work-package or milestone months. Work-package start and end months and milestone months rest on the assumed 48-month duration and are not reproduced here, because no confirmed source carries them. The assumed critical path runs through the data management plan and metadata profile, the joint protocols, the terrestrial campaign and the stress metabolomics on its plots (T1.2, T3.1, T4.1, T5.3).

## Inter-work-package dependencies (PERT)

The structure below is taken from the Phase 3 work-package structure and is part of the assumed design. Each edge is a data input. The Phase 3 structure reports no cycle. WP1 opens the action and holds no upstream dependency. WP3 is the hub the campaign, omics, modelling and exploitation lines draw from.

| From | To | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| WP1 | WP3 | Protocols build on the metadata profile the data management plan fixes (T3.1 on T1.2). |
| WP2 | WP3 | Pipelines implement the integration architecture (T3.4 on T2.3). |
| WP2 | WP4 | Cases are selected and acquisition follows the architecture (T4.1 on T2.5, T4.4 on T2.3). |
| WP3 | WP4 | A campaign starts once the joint protocol exists (T4.1 on T3.1). |
| WP3 | WP5 | Omics sampling follows the protocol and joins through the metadata standard (T5.1 on T3.1, T5.4 on T3.3). |
| WP4 | WP5 | Metabolomics is measured on the terrestrial plots the campaign runs (T5.3 on T4.1). |
| WP3 | WP6 | The training resource is documented against the joint protocol (T6.1 on T3.1). |
| WP4 | WP6 | Models train on the observations the acquisition task produces (T6.3 on T4.4). |
| WP2 | WP7 | The decision surface reads the architecture outputs (T7.2 on T2.3). |
| WP4 | WP7 | A protocol transfers only once it has been run (T7.4 on T4.1). |

## Table 3.1b — Work package descriptions

Task effort is not quantified in person-months, for the reason given above. Each task names its responsible partner, and resources are justified by the capability that carries the work until the effort split is agreed.

### WP1 (lead P01) — Objectives O2
Why needed: the topic sets five coordination duties; WP1 holds four, and the crosswalk interface sits in WP3.
- T1.1 Run consortium governance, reporting and quality management (P01; P02, P10).
- T1.2 Write the shared data management plan and metadata profile (P10; P04, P09). Due M6, before WP3 opens.
- T1.3 Hold the coordination interface to the space-agency earth observation programme the topic names (P02; P12).
- T1.4 Agree cooperation with the named in-situ data frameworks and hold the Joint Research Centre place open (P10; P03, P08). The place counts towards no eligibility condition.
- T1.5 Run ethics, data protection and open science compliance (P01; P11).
Deliverables: D1.1, D1.2, D1.3.

### WP2 (lead P02) — Objectives O1
Why needed: the scope requires the gap analysis to set the integration design, so analysis finishes before the architecture starts.
- T2.1 Prioritise biodiversity knowledge gaps and data needs (P11; P03, P07, P08).
- T2.2 Inventory sensor, platform and omics data streams and metadata state (P02; P09, P10, P12).
- T2.3 Specify the multisensory integration architecture (P02; P04, P10, P12).
- T2.4 Specify socio-ecological and climatic data layers (P11; P07).
- T2.5 Select three demonstration cases against pressure and restoration priority (P11; P03, P07, P08).
Deliverables: D2.1, D2.2, D2.3.

### WP3 (lead P10) — Objectives O2
Why needed: the protocols precede the campaigns, so the three cases produce joinable data.
- T3.1 Agree joint data collection, metadata and processing protocols (P10; P01, P07, P08, P09).
- T3.2 Build occurrence, habitat and ecosystem typology crosswalks (P10; P08, P12).
- T3.3 Define the omics metadata standard and bind it to the occurrence standard (P09; P10).
- T3.4 Build provenance-tracked, reproducible processing pipelines (P04; P09, P12).
- T3.5 Publish datasets and services to the open science cloud and the common data spaces (P10; P04).
- T3.6 Take the harmonisation decisions to the standards bodies (P10; P08, P09).
Deliverables: D3.1, D3.2, D3.3, D3.4.

### WP4 (lead P03) — Objectives O4
Why needed: the three cases sit on one gradient, and each reuse of the terrestrial protocol tests whether an upstream decision transfers.
- T4.1 Run the terrestrial campaign in farmland, grassland and field margins (P03; P01, P02, P06, P11).
- T4.2 Run the freshwater campaign in rivers, floodplains and riparian ecotones (P07; P03, P09, P11).
- T4.3 Run the marine campaign in coastal and benthic habitats (P08; P02, P07, P12).
- T4.4 Acquire and process airborne and satellite observations across the cases (P02; P08, P12). Satellite use draws on the European programmes, as the eligibility condition requires.
- T4.5 Verify which harmonisation decisions survived transfer between realms (P03; P07, P08, P10).
Deliverables: D4.1, D4.2, D4.3, D4.4.

### WP5 (lead P09) — Objectives O1, O4
Why needed: the second expected outcome names three omics layers. Metabolomics comes from P01, and the genomic, transcriptomic and environmental DNA layers from P09.
- T5.1 Design environmental DNA sampling across the three cases (P09; P03, P07, P08).
- T5.2 Run metabarcoding, sequencing and reference library work (P09; P07).
- T5.3 Measure stress metabolomics on farmland and ecotone plots (P01; P03, P09).
- T5.4 Bind the omics layer to in-situ and remote-sensing records (P09; P04, P10).
Deliverables: D5.1, D5.2, D5.3.

### WP6 (lead P12) — Objectives O3, O5
Why needed: the split protocol is fixed before any model is trained, so a benchmark cannot be chosen after the fact to suit a result.
- T6.1 Rework the field archive into documented training and validation sets (P03; P01, P12).
- T6.2 Fix the leakage-safe split protocol and benchmark design (P01; P03, P12). Site, season and treatment travel together into one fold.
- T6.3 Train and benchmark habitat and ecosystem classification models (P12; P02, P07, P08).
- T6.4 Scale the classification to European coverage (P12; P02).
- T6.5 Predict biodiversity trends with stated uncertainty (P12; P01, P11).
Deliverables: D6.1, D6.2, D6.3.

### WP7 (lead P05) — Objectives O6
Why needed: the reporting-needs assessment runs early, so the outputs are shaped to the obligations rather than mapped onto them at the end.
- T7.1 Assess reporting obligations with the competent authorities (P11; P07, P08).
- T7.2 Engineer the decision-support surface carrying biodiversity indicators (P04; P05, P12).
- T7.3 Integrate indicators into farm-management tools and evaluate with users (P05; P03, P04, P06).
- T7.4 Transfer measurement protocols to a second production context (P06; P03, P05).
- T7.5 Run stakeholder engagement, dissemination and exploitation planning (P11; P01, P05, P10).
Deliverables: D7.1, D7.2, D7.3, D7.4.

## Table 3.1c — List of deliverables

Type codes map the canonical deliverable type to the form taxonomy: report to R, dataset to DATA, software to OTHER, other to OTHER. D1.1 is labelled DMP, because it is the data management plan the form requires as its own type within the first six months. Dissemination level is set to PU as an indicative default, consistent with the FAIR and open-science commitment. Datasets carrying sensitive species locations or personal data may be reclassified SEN under the Grant Agreement, with the data management plan (D1.1) deciding.

This timing tension is flagged for resolution rather than concealed.

## Table 3.1e — Critical risks for implementation

These risks are the operator judgement on a design the consortium has not confirmed. Likelihood and severity use Low, Medium and High.

| Risk | Likelihood / Severity | WPs | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R01 The freshwater realm rests on one unconfirmed partner | M / H | WP4, WP5 | Identify a second freshwater partner before the grant agreement. If P07 does not join, the freshwater case is withdrawn and the scope is answered in two realms, stated rather than absorbed. |
| R02 The marine realm rests on one unconfirmed partner | M / H | WP4, WP3 | As R01. Losing P08 also removes the marine occurrence-record contribution, which P10 then carries for the terrestrial and freshwater records only. |
| R03 The consortium geography is thin for a topic asking for use cases across countries | H / M | WP4, WP7 | Ten of twelve partners sit in three country slots. Broaden the user network and the stakeholder work across more countries before submission. |
| R04 The composition condition is met only under assumption | M / H | WP1 | Confirm at least three independent beneficiaries in three countries, one in a Member State, before submission. The Joint Research Centre place counts towards nothing. |
| R05 No methodology vault backs the concept | H / M | WP2, WP6 | Author the methodology before drafting Part B, so the excellence case is lifted from evidence. Until then every mechanism claim stays assumed. |
| R06 A joint protocol is agreed late and a campaign runs under a protocol that changes | M / H | WP3, WP4, WP5 | MS2 gates every campaign. A campaign may not start before the protocol is delivered and adopted in writing. A later change is a recorded revision. |
| R07 The crosswalk does not resolve for some habitats | H / M | WP3 | Report the unresolved labels rather than forcing a mapping, and carry them to the standards bodies. |
| R08 Environmental DNA reference libraries are incomplete for the taxa the cases need | H / M | WP5 | Build reference sequences for the gap taxa inside the project, and report the share of reads that remained unassigned. |
| R09 A field season is lost to weather, access or permitting | M / M | WP4 | Each campaign spans several annual cycles, so one lost season does not end a case. Secure access and permits before the campaign starts. |
| R10 The classification models learn the site rather than the biology | M / H | WP6 | Fix the split protocol in T6.2 before any model is trained. Report benchmarks under the declared split and no other. |
| R11 Practitioners do not act on the indicators | M / M | WP7 | The usability evaluation asks whether a holding could act. A negative result is reported, because an indicator nobody acts on is a finding about the indicator. |
| R12 The budget arrives late or inconsistent with the structure, and Phase 8 stays blocked | M / H | WP1 | This is a lump-sum topic, so the repository computes no figure. Prepare the request as soon as the design is gated, and treat a missing response as a blocking failure. |
| R13 Required satellite data is unavailable from the European programmes for a band or revisit | L / M | WP4, WP6 | The condition permits other data in addition. Record every additional source and the reason the European data did not cover the need. |

## Status and open points

The work-plan structure, the leads, the case-realm assignments, the milestones, the risks and the effort are the operator design intent for a consortium whose participation is not confirmed. They are carried as assumptions, not as evidenced facts. The deliverable titles, types and due months reproduce the canonical reference pack. The detailed budget, the person-month effort and the subcontracting and purchase cost items depend on the validated lump-sum budget and are not finalised here.
